title: sfrecciare
definition: To move or speed past very quickly.

examples.it: Una moto è sfrecciata davanti a noi.
examples.en: A motorcycle sped past us.

note: In the passato prossimo, it normally takes essere (e.g. è sfrecciata).

title: a seconda di / a seconda che
definition: Depending on; depending on whether.

examples.label: A seconda di + noun or pronoun
examples.it: Decideremo a seconda delle circostanze.
examples.en: We'll decide depending on the circumstances.

examples.label: A seconda che + subjunctive clause
examples.it: Vai alla festa? Te lo chiedo perché ci vado a seconda che tu venga o no.
examples.en: Are you going to the party? I'm asking because I'll go depending on whether you come or not.

note: Use 'a seconda di' before a noun or pronoun. 'A seconda che' is rarer, is followed by the subjunctive, and is used when what happens next depends on which of two or more possible situations occurs.

title: azzardare
definition: To dare, venture, or risk saying or doing something despite uncertainty.

examples.it: Non ti azzardare a mettere l'ananas sulla pizza! 🍕
examples.en: Don't you dare put pineapple on pizza! 🍍🚫

note: Besides its transitive use (azzardare un'ipotesi), it is very common in the reflexive form 'azzardarsi', especially in expressions like 'Non ti azzardare a...!' meaning 'Don't you dare...!'.

title: per quanto
definition: Means 'however much', 'no matter how', or 'although', depending on the context.

examples.label: Per quanto + present subjunctive
examples.it: Per quanto ci provi, non riesce a convincerlo.
examples.en: No matter how hard she tries, she can't convince him.

examples.label: Per quanto + imperfect subjunctive
examples.it: Per quanto fosse stanco, ha continuato a lavorare.
examples.en: However tired he was, he kept working.

note: Can introduce either a concession ('although') or indicate degree ('however much'). Pay attention to the context and the verb mood.

title: accorgersi
definition: To notice, realize, or become aware of something.

examples.it: Scusami, non me ne ero accorto.
examples.en: Sorry, I hadn't realized.

examples.label: di + infinitive
examples.it: Mi sto accorgendo di aver sbagliato.
examples.en: I'm beginning to realize I've made a mistake.

examples.label: che + clause
examples.it: Mi sono accorto che Franco l'aveva già fatto ieri.
examples.en: I realized that Franco had already done it yesterday.

note: Always used with essere in compound tenses. It commonly takes 'di' + noun or infinitive when referring to the same subject, or 'che' + a conjugated verb when introducing a separate clause.

title: tanto vale
definition: Means 'might as well', suggesting that one option is the most sensible or worthwhile given the circumstances.

examples.it: Tanto vale andare a piedi.
examples.en: Might as well walk.

examples.label: che + subjunctive
examples.it: A me la crosta della pizza non piace, tanto vale che sia ripiena.
examples.en: I don't like pizza crust, so it might as well be stuffed.

note: 'Tanto vale' is commonly followed by the infinitive, but it can also be followed by 'che' + the subjunctive.

title: anzi
definition: Means 'actually', 'on the contrary', or 'rather'. It is used to correct, strengthen, or replace what has just been said.

examples.it: Non è difficile, anzi è facilissimo.
examples.en: It's not difficult. In fact, it's very easy.

examples.label: To correct yourself
examples.it: Ci vediamo giovedì... anzi, venerdì.
examples.en: See you on Thursday... actually, Friday.

note: 'Anzi' is used to correct, revise or strengthen a previous statement. It often introduces a correction ('actually') or the opposite of what was just said ('on the contrary').

title: ormai
definition: Means 'by now', 'at this point', or 'it's too late now', depending on the context. It indicates that a situation has reached a point where it is unlikely to change.

examples.it: Ormai è troppo tardi per cambiare idea.
examples.en: It's too late to change your mind now.

examples.it: Ormai vivo in Italia da cinque anni.
examples.en: I've lived in Italy for five years now.

note: 'Ormai' often implies that a situation has become established or irreversible. The exact translation depends on the context.

title: capitare
definition: To happen, occur, or come about by chance.

examples.it: Mi è capitato di incontrarlo ieri.
examples.en: I happened to run into him yesterday.

examples.label: capitare che + subjunctive
examples.it: Può capitare che nessuno risponda.
examples.en: It may happen that nobody answers.

note: Use capitare di + infinitive when the person affected is also the understood subject of the infinitive. Use capitare che + subjunctive to introduce a full clause with its own subject.

title: cavarsela
definition: To manage, cope, or get by in a situation.

examples.it: Marco se l'è cavata molto bene all'esame.
examples.en: Marco did very well on the exam.

examples.it: Me la cavo abbastanza bene in italiano.
examples.en: I get by pretty well in Italian.

note: Often used with adverbs like 'bene', 'male', or 'così così'.

title: beccare
definition: To catch, run into, come across, or guess correctly (informal).

examples.it: Ho beccato Marco al supermercato.
examples.en: I ran into Marco at the supermarket.

examples.it: Mi hanno beccato senza biglietto.
examples.en: They caught me without a ticket.

note: A very common informal verb whose exact meaning depends on the context.

title: cadere dal pero
definition: To be caught completely by surprise or to be completely unaware of something.

examples.it: Sono caduto dal pero quando ho saputo che si erano lasciati.
examples.en: I was completely taken aback when I found out they'd broken up.

examples.it: Queste cose me le devi dire in anticipo. Non è bello cadere dal pero davanti alla gente.
examples.en: You need to tell me these things beforehand. It's not nice being caught off guard in front of people.

note: It usually expresses genuine surprise or complete unawareness. It can also be used sarcastically when someone appears surprised by something they should already know.

title: volerci (ci vuole / ci vogliono)
definition: To be needed; to take (time, effort, or resources).

examples.it: Ci vuole molta pazienza per imparare una lingua.
examples.en: It takes a lot of patience to learn a language.

examples.it: Ci vogliono due ore per arrivarci.
examples.en: It takes two hours to get there.

examples.it: C'è voluto molto poco per farlo arrabbiare.
examples.en: It took very little to make him angry.

note: Use the singular (ci vuole) with singular nouns or infinitives, and the plural (ci vogliono) with plural nouns. It often expresses the time, effort, or resources needed for something.

title: avere ragione
definition: Means 'to be right'. It is used to agree that someone is correct, either about a fact, an opinion, or a judgment.

examples.it: Hai ragione, avrei dovuto dirtelo prima.
examples.en: You're right, I should have told you earlier.

examples.it: Secondo me ha ragione Marco.
examples.en: I think Marco is right.

note: Italian uses 'avere ragione' literally 'to have reason' where English uses 'to be right'. The opposite is 'avere torto' ('to be wrong').

title: mica
definition: A very common colloquial adverb used to reinforce a negation, add emphasis, or express contrast. Depending on the context, it can mean 'not at all', 'by no means', or 'it's not as if'.

examples.it: Sono cose vere queste, mica favole.
examples.en: These are real things, not fairy tales.

examples.it: Mica male, questo vino!
examples.en: This wine isn't bad at all!

note: 'Mica' is extremely common in spoken Italian. It often appears with a negative verb (e.g. 'Non è mica facile'), but it can also be used without 'non' to add emphasis or express contrast, as in 'mica favole', 'mica poco', or 'mica male'.

title: sciocchezza
definition: Nonsense, a foolish thing, or something trivial, depending on the context.

examples.it: Sciocchezze, sei bravissimo!
examples.en: Nonsense, you're really good!

examples.it: Non preoccuparti, è una sciocchezza alla fine.
examples.en: Don't worry, it's no big deal after all.

note: Often used in the plural ('sciocchezze') to mean 'nonsense'. It can also refer to something insignificant or foolish. It comes from the adjective 'sciocco' ('foolish', 'silly'), with the suffix '-ezza' forming an abstract noun.

title: farcela
definition: To manage, succeed, or be able to do something.

examples.it: Non ce la faccio più, sono stanchissimo.
examples.en: I can't take it anymore, I'm exhausted.

examples.it: Pensavo di non arrivare in tempo, ma alla fine ce l'ho fatta.
examples.en: I thought I wouldn't make it in time, but in the end I did.

note: 'Farcela' is conjugated with the pronouns 'ce' and 'la': ce la faccio, ce la fai, etc. In compound tenses it takes 'avere', and the past participle agrees with 'la': 'ce l'ho fatta', 'ce l'hai fatta'.

title: si impersonale vs. si passivante
definition: Italian uses 'si' both to make impersonal statements and to form passive constructions. They look similar, but behave differently.

examples.label: Si impersonale
examples.it: In Italia si mangia bene.
examples.en: In Italy, one eats well.

examples.label: Si passivante
examples.it: Si trovano molti tipi di caffè in questo negozio.
examples.en: Many different types of coffee are found in this shop.

note: With the impersonal 'si', there is no grammatical subject and the verb is normally third-person singular. With the passive 'si', the noun is the grammatical subject, so the verb agrees with it: 'si vende una casa' but 'si vendono due case'.

title: potere vs. riuscire vs. farcela
definition: 'Potere', 'riuscire', and 'farcela' can all correspond to 'can' or 'be able to' in English, but they focus on different aspects: possibility, successful execution, and overcoming a difficulty.

examples.label: Potere: possibility or permission
examples.it: Non posso venire stasera perché lavoro.
examples.en: I can't come tonight because I'm working.

examples.label: Riuscire: succeeding in a particular action
examples.it: Non riesco ad aprire questa bottiglia.
examples.en: I can't manage to open this bottle.

examples.label: Farcela: overcoming a difficulty or reaching a goal
examples.it: Pensavo fosse impossibile, ma ce l'ho fatta!
examples.en: I thought it was impossible, but I did it!

note: 'Potere' expresses whether something is possible or permitted, without implying an attempt. 'Riuscire a' focuses on succeeding in performing a particular action. 'Farcela' focuses more on managing to overcome a difficulty or reach a goal, and can stand on its own without stating the action ('Ce la fai?' / 'Ce l'ho fatta!'). 'Riuscire' and 'farcela' often overlap, but 'farcela' is generally more colloquial and expressive.

title: svignarsela
definition: To slip away, sneak off, or make a quick exit, usually without attracting attention.

examples.it: Appena ha visto arrivare la polizia, se l'è svignata.
examples.en: As soon as he saw the police arriving, he slipped away.

examples.it: La festa era noiosa, quindi ce la siamo svignata presto.
examples.en: The party was boring, so we snuck off early.

note: 'Svignarsela' is informal and is commonly used when someone leaves quickly or discreetly. In compound tenses it takes 'essere'. Just like with 'cavarsela', the past participle is always feminine singular ('svignata') because it agrees with 'la': 'me la sono svignata', 'se l'è svignata', 'ce la siamo svignata', etc.

title: caspita
definition: An exclamation expressing surprise, admiration, annoyance, or emphasis, similar to 'wow', 'gosh', or 'damn' depending on the context.

examples.it: Caspita, che bella macchina!
examples.en: Wow, what a beautiful car!

examples.it: Caspita, potevi almeno avvisarmi!
examples.en: Jeez, you could've at least warned me!

note: 'Caspita' is an informal but mild exclamation whose exact meaning depends heavily on tone and context. It can express positive surprise or admiration as well as irritation. It is considerably less vulgar than stronger exclamations such as 'cazzo'.

title: rompere le scatole
definition: To annoy, bother, or pester someone.

examples.it: Smettila di rompermi le scatole!
examples.en: Stop bothering me!

examples.it: Quel rompiscatole continua a chiamarmi.
examples.en: That pain in the neck keeps calling me.

examples.it: Fare tutta questa burocrazia è una rottura di scatole.
examples.en: Dealing with all this bureaucracy is such a pain.

note: 'Rompere le scatole' is an informal but relatively mild expression. 'Scatole' can be replaced by 'palle' or 'coglioni' for increasingly vulgar versions: 'rompere le palle' and 'rompere i coglioni'. The compound noun 'rompiscatole', as well as its more vulgar variants, refers to an annoying or bothersome person. The related expression 'una rottura di scatole' means 'a nuisance' or 'a pain', while the more vulgar 'una rottura di coglioni' corresponds roughly to 'a pain in the ass'.

title: vabbè
definition: A very common informal expression meaning 'well', 'alright', 'oh well', or 'whatever', depending on the context and tone.

examples.it: Vabbè, ne parliamo domani.
examples.en: Alright, we'll talk about it tomorrow.

examples.it: Ho perso l'autobus... vabbè, prenderò il prossimo.
examples.en: I missed the bus... oh well, I'll take the next one.

examples.label: Dismissive
examples.it: Vabbè, fai come vuoi.
examples.en: Whatever, do what you want.

note: 'Vabbè' comes from 'va bene' and is extremely common in informal spoken Italian. Its meaning depends strongly on intonation: it can express acceptance, resignation, dismissal, or a desire to move on. When said dismissively, it can correspond closely to English 'whatever' and may sound rude or annoyed.

title: beh
definition: A very common interjection roughly corresponding to 'well', 'so', or 'then', used to introduce a reaction, conclusion, objection, or question.

examples.label: Introducing a response
examples.it: Che ne pensi? — Beh, è un po' presto per dare un giudizio.
examples.en: What do you think? — Well, it's a bit early to judge.

examples.label: Moving to a conclusion
examples.it: Beh, andiamocene!
examples.en: Well then, let's get out of here!

examples.label: Introducing an objection
examples.it: Beh, piano con certi discorsi!
examples.en: Hey, careful with that kind of talk!

note: 'Beh' is extremely common in spoken Italian and often corresponds to English 'well', though its exact meaning depends on context and intonation. It can introduce a response, move a conversation toward a conclusion ('so', 'then'), or introduce an objection. It derives from 'bene' and is also commonly written 'be''.

title: cagare
definition: Literally 'to shit', but colloquially it can also mean to pay attention to, acknowledge, or give consideration to someone or something.

examples.it: Non mi caga nessuno.
examples.en: Nobody pays any attention to me.

examples.it: Dai, non cagarlo.
examples.en: Come on, don't pay any attention to him.

note: In this figurative use, 'cagare' is vulgar and very informal. It commonly refers to giving someone attention or consideration, especially in negative expressions such as 'non cagare qualcuno'. The pronouns change normally: 'non mi caga', 'non ti caga', 'non lo/la/li/le caga', etc. Its literal meaning is 'to shit'.

title: impazzire
definition: To go crazy or lose one's mind; figuratively, to go wild, become extremely enthusiastic, or start behaving erratically.

examples.it: Sto impazzendo a trovare un parcheggio.
examples.en: I'm going crazy trying to find parking.

examples.it: Quando hanno segnato all'ultimo minuto, lo stadio è impazzito.
examples.en: When they scored in the last minute, the stadium went wild.

examples.label: impazzire per
examples.it: Impazzisco per i romanzi vittoriani.
examples.en: I'm crazy about Victorian novels.

examples.label: For things or devices
examples.it: La bussola è impazzita.
examples.en: The compass has gone haywire.

note: 'Impazzire' can be used literally or figuratively for people, and 'impazzire per qualcuno o qualcosa' means to be crazy about or really love them. It can also describe a device, instrument, or system that starts behaving erratically or stops working properly. In compound tenses it normally takes 'essere': 'sono impazzito/a'.

title: prendersela
definition: To take something personally, get upset, or be offended by something.

examples.it: Dai, non prendertela tanto, stavo scherzando!
examples.en: Come on, don't take it so personally, I was joking!

examples.it: Se l'è presa perché non l'abbiamo invitato.
examples.en: He got upset because we didn't invite him.

examples.label: prendersela con qualcuno
examples.it: Perché te la prendi con me? Non è colpa mia!
examples.en: Why are you taking it out on me? It's not my fault!

note: 'Prendersela' commonly means to get upset or take something personally. 'Prendersela con qualcuno' means to get angry with someone or take one's frustration out on them. In compound tenses it takes 'essere', and the past participle is feminine singular because it agrees with 'la': 'me la sono presa', 'se l'è presa', etc.

title: incazzarsi
definition: To get angry or pissed off.

examples.it: Non ti incazzare, lo sai che è vero!
examples.en: Don't get pissed off, you know it's true!

examples.it: Si è incazzato di brutto perché nessuno l'aveva avvisato.
examples.en: He got seriously pissed off because nobody had told him.

examples.label: Past participle as an adjective
examples.it: È ancora incazzata con me.
examples.en: She's still pissed off at me.

note: 'Incazzarsi' is a very common but vulgar way of saying 'to get angry'. The adjective 'incazzato' means 'angry' or 'pissed off'. It is often used with 'con' for the person someone is angry with: 'Sono incazzato con lui'. The non-pronominal 'incazzare' can also mean 'to piss someone off', as in 'Questa cosa mi incazza'.

title: riferimento vs. referenza
definition: English 'reference' is usually 'riferimento' when it means a mention, allusion, connection, or point of reference. Italian 'referenza' is used in more restricted contexts, such as recommendations, credentials, or professional references.

examples.it: Nessuno ha colto il riferimento. 😔
examples.en: Nobody got the reference. 🕊️

examples.label: referenza
examples.it: Mi hanno chiesto delle referenze per la candidatura. 💼
examples.en: They asked me for references for my application. 👔

note: Don't translate English 'reference' automatically as 'referenza'. For a reference to a film, book, person, idea, or event, use 'riferimento'. 'Referenza' is more limited and is commonly used for recommendations, credentials, or information provided about someone's reliability or professional background. In informal speech, especially among younger speakers and in online contexts, the English borrowing 'reference' can also be heard in place of 'riferimento'.

title: prenderci la mano
definition: To get the hang of something or become comfortable and skilled at doing it through practice.

examples.it: All'inizio è difficile, devi solo prenderci la mano.
examples.en: It's difficult at first, you just need to get the hang of it.

examples.it: Una volta che ci hai preso la mano, diventa molto più facile.
examples.en: Once you get the hang of it, it becomes much easier.

note: 'Prenderci la mano' is used when someone gradually becomes familiar or proficient with something through practice. The 'ci' is part of the expression and refers to the activity or situation: 'ci prendo la mano', 'ci hai preso la mano', etc. Don't confuse it with the literal 'prendere la mano' ('to take someone's hand').

title: saperci fare
definition: To know how to handle something or someone; to have a knack or be skilled at dealing with a particular person, activity, or situation.

examples.it: Non ti preoccupare, nonna, lui ci sa fare con i computer.
examples.en: Don't worry, grandma, he knows his way around computers.

examples.it: Essere attraente non significa saperci fare a letto.
examples.en: Being attractive doesn't mean you're good in bed.

note: 'Saperci fare' means to have skill, ability, or a particular knack for dealing with someone or something. It is commonly used with 'con': 'saperci fare con qualcuno/qualcosa'. It can also stand on its own or be used with other complements when the context makes the relevant skill clear. The pronoun 'ci' is a fixed part of the expression: 'io ci so fare', 'tu ci sai fare', 'lui/lei ci sa fare', etc.

title: desolato
definition: Desolate, bleak, or deserted. When referring to a person, it can also mean deeply sorry, saddened, or distressed.

examples.it: Dopo l'incendio, il paesaggio era completamente desolato.
examples.en: After the fire, the landscape was completely desolate.

examples.label: Sono desolato
examples.it: Sono desolato, ma non posso aiutarla.
examples.en: I'm terribly sorry, but I can't help you.

examples.label: Deeply saddened
examples.it: Era desolato per quello che era successo.
examples.en: He was deeply upset about what had happened.

note: When describing a place, 'desolato' can mean 'desolate', 'bleak', or 'deserted'. With a person, however, 'sono desolato/a' is commonly used to express strong regret or sorrow and can correspond to 'I'm terribly sorry'. It is generally stronger and more formal than 'mi dispiace'.

title: tanto va la gatta al lardo che ci lascia lo zampino
definition: If you repeatedly take the same risk or do something you shouldn't, sooner or later you'll get caught or suffer the consequences.

examples.it: Continua pure a copiare agli esami, ma ricorda: tanto va la gatta al lardo che ci lascia lo zampino.
examples.en: Keep cheating on exams if you want, but remember: sooner or later you'll get caught.

note: Literally, 'the cat goes to the lard so often that eventually she leaves her paw behind.' The proverb warns that repeatedly taking the same risk will eventually have consequences. Depending on the context, English equivalents include 'you can only push your luck so far' and 'play with fire long enough and you'll get burned'.

title: marachella
definition: A mischievous or naughty little act, especially one done by a child; a prank or bit of mischief.

examples.it: Da piccolo ne combinavo di marachelle.
examples.en: When I was little, I used to get up to all sorts of mischief.

examples.it: I bambini hanno fatto una marachella mentre la mamma era distratta.
examples.en: The children got into some mischief while their mother was distracted.

note: 'Marachella' usually refers to relatively harmless mischief or naughty behaviour, especially by children, and often has a playful or affectionate tone. A common expression is 'combinare una marachella' ('to get up to mischief' or 'to do something naughty'). The plural is 'marachelle'.

title: tarallucci e vino
definition: An expression used for the amicable resolution of an argument, dispute, or difficult situation, sometimes with the implication that a serious matter has been smoothed over too conveniently.

examples.it: Dopo ore di discussione, è finita a tarallucci e vino.
examples.en: After hours of arguing, in the end everyone made peace.

examples.it: Erano pronti a farsi causa per un parcheggio, poi è finita a tarallucci e vino.
examples.en: They were ready to sue each other over a parking spot, but in the end they made peace.

note: The expression is most commonly used in the construction 'finire a tarallucci e vino', meaning that a disagreement or difficult situation ends with everyone making peace. Literally, 'tarallucci e vino' means 'taralli and wine', evoking people settling their differences over food and drink. It can be used neutrally or humorously for an unexpectedly friendly resolution, but it can also have a critical or ironic tone, suggesting that a serious matter was conveniently smoothed over without any real consequences.

title: tra il dire e il fare c'è di mezzo il mare
definition: It's much easier to say that you will do something than to actually do it; there can be a big gap between words and actions.

examples.it: Dice che aprirà un ristorante entro l'anno, ma tra il dire e il fare c'è di mezzo il mare.
examples.en: He says he'll open a restaurant by the end of the year, but saying it and actually doing it are two very different things.

examples.it: «Da domani mi sveglio alle sei e vado a correre ogni mattina.» «Certo... tra il dire e il fare c'è di mezzo il mare.»
examples.en: "Starting tomorrow, I'm getting up at six and going running every morning." "Sure... easier said than done."

note: Literally, 'between saying and doing lies the sea.' The proverb emphasizes the distance between intentions or promises and actually putting them into practice. A common English equivalent is 'easier said than done', although the Italian proverb can also carry the broader idea that words and actions are two very different things.

title: cazzeggiare
definition: To mess around, waste time, or do nothing particularly useful or serious, often in a relaxed or enjoyable way.

examples.it: Carlo passa tutto il tempo a cazzeggiare invece di studiare.
examples.en: Carlo spends all his time messing around instead of studying.

examples.it: Stasera non ho voglia di fare niente, voglio solo cazzeggiare con gli amici.
examples.en: I don't feel like doing anything tonight, I just want to hang around and mess about with my friends.

note: 'Cazzeggiare' is a very common informal verb derived from 'cazzo'. Despite its vulgar origin, it is often used quite casually to mean wasting time, fooling around, or doing things without any serious purpose. The related noun 'cazzeggiamento' refers to the activity itself: 'Basta con il cazzeggiamento, mettiamoci al lavoro!' ('Enough messing around, let's get to work!'). Its tone depends heavily on context, so it is best avoided in formal situations.

title: cazziare
definition: To tell someone off, scold them, or give them a dressing-down.

examples.it: Mia madre mi ha cazziato perché sono tornato a casa tardissimo.
examples.en: My mother told me off because I came home really late.

examples.label: cazziatone
examples.it: Ha cercato di nascondere le tracce per evitare il cazziatone del capo.
examples.en: He tried to cover his tracks to avoid getting a massive telling-off from his boss.

note: 'Cazziare' is an informal and vulgar verb meaning to scold or reprimand someone, often quite harshly. The related noun 'cazziata' means a telling-off or dressing-down, as in 'Mi sono preso una cazziata' ('I got a telling-off'). 'Cazziatone' is the augmentative form and refers to an especially severe or lengthy telling-off.

title: la superbia andò a cavallo e tornò a piedi
definition: Pride and arrogance often lead to humiliation or downfall.

examples.it: Era sicuro di vincere, ma è arrivato ultimo. La superbia andò a cavallo e tornò a piedi.
examples.en: He was sure he'd win, but he came last. Pride comes before a fall.

note: Literally, 'pride went out on horseback and came back on foot.' The proverb is used when someone's arrogance or excessive confidence ends in humiliation or defeat. A close English equivalent is 'pride comes before a fall', a shortened form of the biblical 'Pride goeth before destruction, and an haughty spirit before a fall' (Proverbs 16:18, KJV).
